title: Loss Functions
overview: A loss function turns prediction error into a single number the optimizer can minimize. Matching the loss to the task and output distribution matters for stable training.
objectives: Pick a loss for regression, classification and imbalanced data

method.title: Regression losses
method.body: MSE penalizes large errors strongly; MAE and Huber are more robust to outliers.

method.title: Cross-entropy
method.body: Measures the negative log probability assigned to the true class and is the standard classification loss.

method.title: Logits and stability
method.body: Combine softmax and log in one step (log-sum-exp) to avoid numerical overflow.

method.title: Imbalance
method.body: Class weights or focal loss can down-weight easy, frequent examples.

pseudocode:
mse = mean((y_hat - y)**2)
logp = z - logsumexp(z)
ce = -mean(logp[range(N), y])
bce = -mean(y*log(p) + (1-y)*log(1-p))

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
logits = np.array([[2.0, 0.5, -1.0], [0.1, 0.2, 3.0]])
labels = np.array([0, 2])
z = logits - logits.max(axis=1, keepdims=True)
logp = z - np.log(np.exp(z).sum(axis=1, keepdims=True))
ce = -logp[np.arange(2), labels].mean()
print("cross-entropy:", round(float(ce), 4))
print("mse:", np.mean((np.array([1.0, 2.0]) - np.array([1.5, 1.0])) ** 2))
